 # PT-502
 
-Physical Therapy Society member portal, built with Rails and PostgreSQL.
-
-## Help and training
-
-Once the app is running, choose **Help** in the navigation, or open:
-
-- `/help/member`: sign-in, profiles, points, events, attendance, and outside-event requests.
-- `/help/officer`: member management, dues, points, roles, events, and approvals (officers only).
-- `/help/system`: installation, Heroku operations, backups, import recovery, rollback, and costs (officers only).
-
-Before installation, open [the system guide](docs/system-guide.html) in a browser.
-It is the same document served in the app. It includes local setup and initial
-manager setup using `system:bootstrap`; no private settings are stored in it.
-
-For feature changes, use [the help maintenance checklist](docs/help-maintenance.md).
-Screenshots contain fictional training data.
-
-## Checks
-
-Use Ruby from `.ruby-version` and PostgreSQL. After local setup:
-
-```sh
-bundle exec rails db:prepare
-RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec rails db:prepare
-bundle exec rspec spec/
-bundle exec rubocop
-node --test spec/javascript/location_controllers_test.cjs
-```
-
-The test database is `pt502_test` and is disposable. The Procfile starts Puma
-and runs migrations during a Heroku release; it does not seed or import member data.

Member guide

-

Use this guide on your first visit, or choose a task below. You can read it before signing in.

-
-

On this page

-
    -
  • Sign in and sign out
    • -
  • Finish or edit your profile
    • -
  • Understand points and active status
    • -
  • Find events and save them to your calendar
    • -
  • Check in at an event
    • -
  • Submit an outside event and follow its status
    • -
  • Troubleshooting
    • -
  • Practice with a new member
    • -
-
-
-

Sign in and sign out

-
    -
  1. Open the club’s website. Choose Sign up with Google on your first visit, or Sign in with Google when returning.
    2. -
  2. Select your @tamu.edu Google account. A personal account cannot sign in.
    3. -
  3. On your first visit, finish the required profile fields. Returning members go to Home.
    4. -
  4. When finished on a shared device, choose Sign out in the top navigation.
    5. -
- <%= render "screenshot", name: "sign-in", caption: "The sign-in page has separate buttons for returning and new members." %> -
-
-

Finish or edit your profile

-
    -
  1. For an existing profile, open the menu beside your name and choose Edit my profile.
    2. -
  2. Enter your first and last names and choose an Expected graduation term.
    3. -
  3. Choose your Anticipated application cycle. These choices are summers, such as Summer 2027.
    4. -
  4. Check I am available to carpool for field trips if you can help with rides.
    5. -
  5. Sharing a phone number is optional. Check Share my phone number with officers to show the phone field, then enter a number with 10–15 digits. Spaces, parentheses, dashes, and an initial + are allowed.
    6. -
  6. Choose Save profile. Look for Profile saved. and check your details on Home.
    7. -
-

Turning phone sharing off removes your saved number when you save. Officers can see carpool availability and a shared number, but cannot change your phone number or sharing choice. You cannot change your own role or award yourself points.

- <%= render "screenshot", name: "profile", caption: "Choose a graduation term and a summer application cycle; carpool and phone sharing are optional." %> -
-
-

Understand points and active status

-
    -
  1. Open Home. Total points shows earned points followed by the semester’s required total.
    2. -
  2. Read each required point type separately. Meeting the total alone does not satisfy a missing type minimum.
    3. -
  3. Read the status badge and the messages below it. Active membership requires the total, every required type minimum, and paid semester dues.
    4. -
  4. If points or dues look wrong, tell an officer the event name, date, and expected point type. Officers record dues; there is no payment checkout in this app.
    5. -
-

Approved outside events and successful attendance check-ins add points. Pending or denied submissions do not. Home shows your own information; regular members cannot open the officer member list.

- <%= render "screenshot", name: "member-home", caption: "Home shows dues and point shortfalls, profile details, and your recent outside-event submissions." %> -
-
-

Find events and save them to your calendar

-
    -
  1. Choose Events, or open an upcoming event from Home.
    2. -
  2. Open an event to check its location, time, description, point type, and point value.
    3. -
  3. Choose Download .ics and open the downloaded file in your calendar, or choose Add to Google Calendar and save the event there.
    4. -
-

Saving a calendar event does not check you in or award points. If there are no events, check again when officers publish the next meeting.

- <%= render "screenshot", name: "event", caption: "An event’s details include its attendance action and both calendar options." %> -
-
-

Check in at an event

-
    -
  1. At the venue, scan the officer’s QR code, or open the event and choose Attend Meeting.
    2. -
  2. Sign in and finish your profile if asked. Stay near the meeting location.
    3. -
  3. Choose Check in using my location and allow this website to use your device’s location.
    4. -
  4. Wait for You’re marked present. The page shows the points awarded and your updated total.
    5. -
-

The page tells you the allowed distance. Your coordinates are used for the distance check and are not stored with attendance. A second check-in for the same event does not earn a second award.

- <%= render "screenshot", name: "check-in", caption: "The check-in page explains the venue radius and asks for location access." %> -
-
-

Submit an outside event and follow its status

-
    -
  1. On Home, find Non-PT event submissions and choose Submit an event.
    2. -
  2. Enter the event name, the date you attended, a point type, and a description or proof of attendance. The date cannot be in the future. The proof field accepts text; it is not a file upload.
    3. -
  3. Choose Submit for approval. Look for the confirmation that your submission was sent.
    4. -
  4. Return to Home to see the request as Pending. The latest ten submissions appear here.
    5. -
  5. After review, Approved means points were added. Denied includes the officer’s reason and adds no points.
    6. -
-

Do not submit the same event and date again to chase an update. Ask an officer about an older request or a correction; the app has no member edit or cancel action for submitted requests.

- <%= render "screenshot", name: "submission", caption: "The outside-event form asks for the name, date, point type, and written description or proof." %> - <%= render "screenshot", name: "submission-status", caption: "Home lists pending, approved, and denied submissions, including the denial reason." %> -
-
-

Troubleshooting

-
-
Google sign-in fails or chooses the wrong account
Return to the sign-in page and select your @tamu.edu account. If Google reports a service error, retry later. If it reports a redirect or configuration error, send an officer the message and time; changing your profile will not fix it. Never send passwords or sign-in codes.
-
A profile field is highlighted or saving fails
Use the error links at the top to reach each field. Fill every required field, choose a summer cycle, and correct the phone number if sharing it. Retry after a save error. Previously saved details stay in place until a valid save succeeds.
-
Location is denied, times out, or says you are too far away
Allow location for this site in your browser’s site settings, enable device location, move closer to the venue, and try again. Use the club’s secure website in your usual browser. Ask an officer to check the event’s coordinates if the problem continues.
-
Check-in is not configured
Ask the event officer to configure the venue. Reopening or repeatedly submitting the page will not fix missing coordinates.
-
A submission does not go through
Read the errors, fill all four fields, select an available type, and check the date. If it says you already submitted the event, look on Home. After a connection or server error, check Home before retrying so you do not create another request.
-
Points are missing or status is still inactive
Check whether a request is still pending or denied, whether a type minimum is missing, and whether dues are recorded. A calendar entry alone earns no points. Refresh Home after a successful review or check-in, then contact an officer with the event details.
-
A calendar download fails
Return to the event and retry Download .ics. If your browser blocked the download, allow it for this site. Add to Google Calendar is the other available option.
-
A page is unavailable or you are not authorized
Sign in again and finish your profile. Officer pages require an officer role. If a normal member page still fails, send an officer the page name, message, and time, with private details removed.
-
-
-
-

Practice with a new member

-

Allow about 10 minutes. Have the learner explain each step back to you.

-
    -
  1. Sign in with their account and save the required profile details. Let them choose whether to share their phone.
    2. -
  2. Find their total, one type minimum, and their dues status on Home. Explain what is still needed to be active.
    3. -
  3. Open a published event and save it to a calendar.
    4. -
  4. At a real meeting, complete check-in once and find the confirmation.
    5. -
  5. Submit a genuine outside event, or explain the form without submitting fictional work. Find its pending status after sending.
    6. -
  6. Find the troubleshooting entry for denied location access, then sign out.
    7. -
-
-

Member information, dues, and points

-
    -
  1. Choose Members. Regular members and officers appear in separate tables.
    2. -
  2. Read carpool availability, graduation, and application cycle. Not shared means a phone number is unavailable; do not ask another officer to reveal it.
    3. -
  3. Choose Edit profile for a member, correct their details, and choose Save profile. Phone number and consent stay under the member’s control.
    4. -
  4. To record payment received outside the app, check Paid dues. It saves when changed. Clear it only to correct the record, then verify the saved state after refreshing.
    5. -
  5. To correct points, enter the intended absolute total for that point type in the member’s row, then leave the field to save. Entering 3 sets that type to 3; it does not add 3. Use a whole number of zero or more, then refresh to verify it.

  6. Check the member’s total and status. Dues and every point minimum must be satisfied for the table to show Active.

- <%= render "screenshot", name: "members", caption: "The member table keeps dues, per-type point controls, status, and profile links together; officers are listed separately." %> - <%= render "screenshot", name: "officer-profile", caption: "An officer can edit profile details without changing a member’s phone-sharing choice." %> -

Manager-only role changes

-

The app labels officer roles Admin and Manager. Both can use ordinary officer tools. Only Managers can change Member/Admin roles and point requirements.

-
    -
  1. As a Manager, open Members and find the person in the correct table.
    2. -
  2. Choose Promote to Admin to grant officer tools to a Member, or Demote to Member to remove Admin tools. Confirm the prompt.
    3. -
  3. Confirm the person moves to the correct table and their role label changes.
    4. -
-

You cannot change your own role or a Manager’s role here. The buttons do not create another Manager. Follow the club’s agreed access process for those changes.

-

Create, edit, and delete events

-
    -
  1. Choose Create Event on Home or Events.
    2. -
  2. Fill in the name, description, date and time, and location. If you add an end time, it must be after the start.
    3. -
  3. Set both venue coordinates for check-in, or leave both blank to configure later. Use my current location fills the fields only; use it while at the actual venue, not at home.
    4. -
  4. Set a positive check-in radius in meters, a point value of zero or more, and a point type. If the type is Other, fill in the additional type detail.
    5. -
  5. Choose Save Event, then check the published details.
    6. -
  6. For a correction, open the event, choose Edit, change the fields, and save. Use Delete only when the event should be removed and confirm the prompt.
    7. -
-

Deleting an event also removes its attendance records. Discuss deleting an event with attendance already recorded before proceeding. Calendar files people already saved do not automatically update.

QR codes and attendance

-
    -
  1. Open the event and check the venue coordinates and allowed radius.
    2. -
  2. Choose Show check-in QR code. Display that page at the meeting; members can scan the code or use its check-in link.
    3. -
  3. Ask members to allow location access and look for their marked-present confirmation. Opening the link alone does not record attendance.
    4. -
  4. Return to the event and choose Refresh attendance to see names and check-in times.
    5. -
-

The app checks distance and awards each member once per event. There is no manual attendance toggle on this page. For an exceptional missing award, verify attendance and correct the member’s point-type total if club policy permits.

- <%= render "screenshot", name: "qr", caption: "Display the event-specific QR code or share the check-in link at the venue." %> - <%= render "screenshot", name: "attendance", caption: "The officer event page lists marked-present members and their check-in times." %> -

Approve or deny outside events

-
    -
  1. Choose Point Requests. The approval queue shows pending requests with the member, event, date, type, and written proof.
    2. -
  2. Check the details against the club’s point policy. In the approval field, enter a positive whole number and choose Approve.
    3. -
  3. To deny instead, enter a reason in Reason (required) and choose Deny.
    4. -
  4. Look for the decision’s confirmation. A reviewed request leaves the pending queue; the member sees the decision on Home.
    5. -
-

Approval adds points to the selected type. Denial adds none and shows your reason to the member. The current queue lists pending work; it has no status filter or reviewed-request history screen. If another officer already decided, refresh rather than repeat the award through the member table.

- <%= render "screenshot", name: "requests", caption: "Each pending request has separate approval points and required denial-reason controls." %> -

Manager-only point requirements

-
    -
  1. As a Manager, choose Point requirements.
    2. -
  2. Enter the total required points and each type’s minimum, using whole numbers of zero or more. Zero means that minimum is not required.
    3. -
  3. Choose Save requirements. Members’ status is calculated using the new requirements.
    4. -
  4. To add a type, fill in its unique name and minimum in Add a point type, then choose Add point type.
    5. -
  5. Delete an unused, non-core type with its Delete button and confirm. Service, Professionalism, and Other are core types and cannot be deleted here. A type used by events or points cannot be deleted.
    6. -
-

Confirm a semester-policy change with the club before saving. Changing a minimum does not change points already earned.

- <%= render "screenshot", name: "requirements", caption: "Managers set the overall minimum, individual type minimums, and additional point types." %> -

Troubleshooting

-
-
A role or settings control is missing
Check the role badge. Admins cannot use Manager-only controls. A regular Member cannot use officer tools. Ask an existing Manager to verify access; do not borrow another person’s sign-in.
-
A profile edit fails
Correct the highlighted required fields and choose a summer cycle. Previous saved details remain unchanged after an invalid save. Ask the member to correct their own shared phone if it is invalid; officers cannot edit it.
-
Points or dues do not save
Refresh and check the current value before retrying. Set points to the desired type total, not an amount to add. Use a nonnegative whole number in a currently available point type’s field, then leave the field to save.
-
An event does not save
Read the errors above the form. Fill required fields, provide both coordinates or neither, use a positive radius, and check the end time. Other requires its extra description. A location button failure leaves manual coordinate entry available.
-
Attendance cannot load or nobody can check in
Choose Refresh attendance or Try again. Verify the meeting’s coordinates at the venue and its radius. Ask members to allow location and use the secure club URL. Do not create another event just to retry.
-
There are no pending requests
This can mean all requests have been reviewed. Ask the member to check the status on Home. If the queue reports a load error, try again before assuming it is empty.
